extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans and researchers interested in television/comedy production and the series Drunk History
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive standards for producing or evaluating Drunk History–style television episodes: short (≈22 min) comedic reenactments of historical anecdotes told by inebriated narrators, with attention to factual accuracy, rehearsal practice, ethical treatment of storytellers, and production values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode format: inebriated narrator with reenactments and lip sync
rubrics_metrics.description: In each episode, an inebriated narrator, joined by host Waters, struggles to recount an event from history, while actors enact the narrator's anecdotes and also lip sync the dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use actors to physically reenact the story and to lip sync the (imperfect) narration; the juxtaposition of drunken verbal storytelling and staged pantomime is the show's central format and comedic device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: research and rehearsal before intoxication
rubrics_metrics.description: The storytellers in the series read up on the stories while sober, then rehearse it in front of a producer before getting drunk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require storytellers to be informed about the events beforehand and to rehearse with production staff to ensure a usable narrative framework despite later intoxication; this practice preserves core story structure and factual anchors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host participation / ethical practice toward storytellers
rubrics_metrics.description: Waters says he drinks with the storytellers in order to 'let them know we're doing this together' and so as not to make it feel exploitative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers should participate or otherwise take steps to avoid exploiting intoxicated participants; make efforts to create a consensual, respectful environment when recording inebriated narrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy of dates and story elements
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Derek Waters, all the dates and story elements are true, though the historical figures' dialogue is obviously not accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that names, dates and core factual elements are checked and presented accurately even if dialogue and phrasing are fictionalized; Waters: 'Make sure you say this date or this person's name. I don't want to mess up anyone's names.' Independent newspapers have verified the series' historical information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted creative license in dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: The historical figures' dialogue is obviously not accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue and conversational lines for reenacted characters may be invented for comedic effect; preserve factual backbone while allowing fictionalized speech to enhance humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode length / running time constraint
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format episodes to fit a ~22-minute half-hour TV slot; pacing and segment length should respect this runtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception measures (aggregated ratings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotten Tomatoes approval rating and average score; Metacritic weighted average score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use aggregator scores (e.g., Rotten Tomatoes approval %, average score; Metacritic weighted average) and critics' consensus as common metrics for critical reception; note critics' qualitative summaries (e.g., 'boozy lectures wear out their welcome fast...') as indicators of perceived pacing or stylistic weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreliance on cheesy pantomime / pacing concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics' consensus: 'Drunk History's boozy lectures wear out their welcome fast and the bevy of comedic talent is wasted on cheesy pantomimes...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious of extended or repetitive pantomime that can dilute comedic impact; ensure comedic talent is used effectively and pacing keeps segments fresh to avoid viewer fatigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production-value excellence (cinematography, costumes, editing, production design, directing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The show received awards and nominations for cinematography, costumes, picture editing, production design and directing (several Emmy nominations; wins in cinematography and costumes; Art Directors Guild award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality cinematography, costumes, picture editing, production design and directing are recognized standards for the series; excellence in these areas contributes to industry recognition and should be prioritized in production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability for international/local versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple international versions have been produced (UK, Latin America, Hungary, Brazil, Argentina, Poland, Australia, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format is adaptable across markets and languages; local hosts and cultural tailoring (choice of historical subjects, presenters) are used when producing regional versions while retaining core format (drunk narrator + reenactment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Web-to-television adaptation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The series is based on the Funny or Die web series of the same name created by Derek Waters in 2007; the first video premiered online and later the format transferred to TV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adapting from web shorts to TV, retain the essential conceit while expanding structure/production to fit broadcast constraints; successful transition involves scaling production values and episode structure for network release.
